subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: For plain `message.send`, should OpenClaw prevent models from seeing poll content fields in the send schema, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: Current code intentionally accepts schema-padded poll metadata but rejects non-empty poll content fields on send; changing that boundary affects shared channel delivery semantics across Feishu, Telegram, Discord, Slack, and other message-tool channels.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

options.title: Strip on send
options.body: Treat `action: "send"` as authoritative and drop poll fields before delivery, improving reliability but potentially masking poll intent mistakes.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields on send and require callers or schema discovery to avoid generating them accidentally.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question is a shared model-facing tool contract decision, and the existing review discussion plus prior message-tool schema split history make this the best available routing candidate.
